name: dotnet-msix

Packages MSIX apps: creation, signing, Microsoft Store submission, App Installer sideload/auto-update, bundles, and CI/CD for .NET desktop apps.

Scope: Windows App SDK 1.6+; Windows 10 build 19041+ minimum for MSIX with Windows App SDK; Windows 10 build 1709+ for App Installer auto-update protocol; .NET 8.0+ baseline. Supports csproj (`WindowsPackageType`), WAP projects, self-signed/trusted CA/Store signing, Store, App Installer, SCCM/Intune, App Installer XML, differential updates, and `.msixbundle` multi-architecture. See [skill:dotnet-winui], [skill:dotnet-native-aot], [skill:dotnet-gha-patterns], [skill:dotnet-ado-patterns], [skill:dotnet-nuget-authoring], [skill:dotnet-containers], and [references/detailed-examples.md](references/detailed-examples.md).

Modern WinUI 3/Windows App SDK apps can produce MSIX directly from `.csproj`; WPF/WinForms apps use a Visual Studio “Windows Application Packaging Project” (`.wapproj`) with:
`<ProjectReference Include="..\MyWpfApp\MyWpfApp.csproj" />`
`<DefaultLanguage>en-US</DefaultLanguage>`
`<AppxPackageDir>$(SolutionDir)AppPackages\</AppxPackageDir>`

Typical csproj:
`<TargetFramework>net8.0-windows10.0.19041.0</TargetFramework>`
`<UseWinUI>true</UseWinUI>`
`<WindowsPackageType>MSIX</WindowsPackageType>`
`<AppxPackageDir>$(SolutionDir)AppPackages\</AppxPackageDir>`
`<GenerateAppxPackageOnBuild>false</GenerateAppxPackageOnBuild>`

Build the MSIX package:
dotnet publish --configuration Release --runtime win-x64 \

All MSIX packages must be signed to install on Windows. The signing certificate's Subject must match the `Publisher` attribute in the package manifest.

$cert = New-SelfSignedCertificate `
-Subject "CN=My Company, O=My Company, L=Seattle, S=WA, C=US" `
-FriendlyName "MyApp Dev Signing" `
-CertStoreLocation "Cert:\CurrentUser\My" `
-TextExtension @("<REDACTED_IP>={text}<REDACTED_IP>.<REDACTED_IP>.3", `
"<REDACTED_IP>={text}")
$password = ConvertTo-SecureString -String "$env:CERT_PASSWORD" -Force -AsPlainText
Export-PfxCertificate -Cert $cert `
-FilePath "MyApp_DevSigning.pfx" `
$signtool = Get-ChildItem "C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\bin\*\x64\signtool.exe" |
Sort-Object { [version]($_.Directory.Parent.Name) } -Descending |
Select-Object -First 1 -ExpandProperty FullName
& $signtool sign /fd SHA256 /a /f "MyApp_DevSigning.pfx" `
/p "$env:CERT_PASSWORD" `
"AppPackages\MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix"

For production distribution outside the Microsoft Store:
1. **Obtain a code signing certificate** from a trusted CA (DigiCert, Sectigo, GlobalSign)
2. **Subject must match** the `Publisher` in `Package.appxmanifest`
3. **Timestamp the signature** for long-term validity

& signtool.exe sign /fd SHA256 /sha1 "THUMBPRINT_HERE" `
/tr http://timestamp.digicert.com /td SHA256 `
"AppPackages\MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix"
& signtool.exe sign /fd SHA256 /f "production-cert.pfx" `
/p "$env:CERT_PASSWORD" `
/tr http://timestamp.digicert.com /td SHA256 `
"AppPackages\MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix"

Store apps are re-signed by Microsoft; no production signing certificate is needed for Store-only distribution. Store workflow: register at https://partner.microsoft.com/dashboard, reserve the app name, build with Store association, then submit the `.msixupload` through Partner Center.

App Installer (`.appinstaller`) supports hosted direct distribution and auto-update via web server, network share, or CDN. Users install via:
ms-appinstaller:?source=https://mycompany.com/apps/MyApp.appinstaller

Update settings include `HoursBetweenUpdateChecks`, `ShowPrompt`, `UpdateBlocksActivation`, `AutomaticBackgroundTask`, and `ForceUpdateFromAnyVersion`. Differential updates are automatic when the same `PackageName` and `Publisher` are used.

Custom checks use `Package.Current.CheckUpdateAvailabilityAsync()`.

Enterprise deployment supports Intune, SCCM/MECM, Group Policy, and PowerShell:
Add-AppxPackage -Path "\\fileserver\apps\MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix"
Add-AppxProvisionedPackage -Online `
-PackagePath "MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix"
